title: Link
summary: A Machine is one worfy data folder. Link two Machines with a 6-digit code, and each can open the other's Projects when that Machine allows it. A Project still runs on its own Machine: your window shows it and sends commands. The link works on the local network, and through Tailscale when both sides turn it on.

scene.description: Two linked Machines. Under This Machine: the Machine, the Machines section of its sidebar and your window. Under Other Machine: the Linked machine, the access it gives this one, and its Project. The Machine is linked to the other by a 6-digit code. The Machines section shows the state of the Linked machine. Your window sends commands to the other Machine; while its switch “Linked machines can work with my Projects” is on, the access level it gives this Machine decides what reaches the Project, and the Project is shown in your window.

labels.step1: Open Link a machine… on both worfy. On one, pick the other and type the 6-digit code it shows. The link works both ways.
labels.step2: The Machines section in the sidebar lists the Linked machine as Online, Sleeping, Offline or Certificate changed. worfy reconnects by itself.
labels.step3: The Machine that owns the Projects decides in Settings → Machines. “Linked machines can work with my Projects” is off by default; while it is on, each Linked machine gets Off, Read only or Full access. A new link starts at Off.
labels.step4: A click on its Project in the sidebar opens it in your window. Sessions, Terminals and Autopilot run over there; your window shows them and sends commands.

flow.description: The data flow of a call from your window to a Project of Linked machine M. The window reads the channel's access mark: local and link channels stay with this Machine's own handlers, project and desktop ones go as linked.invoke to the linked handlers of this Machine's main. RemoteCalls sends the call as a frame over M's current connection. On M, the link service passes it to the IPC adapter, which runs the same handler a window on M would, if the mark and the access level allow it. The answer and M's events come back as frames; RemoteCalls parses them with this side's schema, and they reach the window as the answer and as linked.event.

labels.handlerNote: as a window on M calls

text: A Linked machine's call runs the same IPC handler as a window's, with the same schemas. A channel name the adapter does not know is closed, and Read only refuses every project channel marked write.
Pairing is SPAKE2 with the code as the password, bound to both certificate fingerprints, so a machine in the middle makes it fail.

files.src/main/link/ipc-adapter.ts: Calls from one: the mark and level checks
files.src/shared/ipc/channels.ts: The access mark of each channel
files.src/renderer/ipc.ts: Routes a window's call by its mark

limits: A code lives 2 minutes, and the first attempt burns it. 10 failed attempts in a row, or within an hour, close linking.
A message on a connection is at most 16 MiB, and a call waits 30 seconds for its answer.
Without Link through Tailscale on at both ends, only the local network and loopback get through. There is no relay.
